transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

STOP EVERYTHING IMMEDIATELY. This is an electrical hazard.

1. DO NOT touch the washing machine or go near the water if you are standing in it.
2. Go to your main fuse box/consumer unit and SWITCH OFF THE MAIN POWER SUPPLY TO THE HOUSE (or at least the kitchen circuit) immediately. Do not try to unplug it from the socket if there is water around it—that could electrocute you.
3. Once the power is off, you can safely approach the machine.

### After Power is Off:

1. Stop the wash cycle: If you turned off the main power, the machine has stopped. If you only switched off a plug (which I advise against due to water), press "Start/Pause" or turn the dial to "Off."
2. Do not try to move the heavy washing machine while it is full of water and on a slippery floor—it could tip over or cause further damage.
3. Call a professional plumber or appliance repair technician. This is likely a failed hose, pump issue, or internal leak that needs expert diagnosis.
4. Dry up the visible water carefully with towels to prevent slip hazards and further water damage to your cabinets, but only if it’s safe to do so after power is off.

### Important Notes:
• Water + Electricity = Danger. Even after turning off the main power, wait a few minutes before touching anything wet near electrical components.
• Do not use the washing machine again until it has been inspected and repaired by a qualified professional.
• If you have any doubt about your ability to safely turn off the main power, leave the house and call emergency services or a licensed electrician/plumber immediately.

Your safety is the top priority. Please act quickly but calmly.
